Explanation: RAM: Random Access Memory. Primary storage — holds data/programs currently in use. Volatile (data lost when power off). Faster than hard disk. More RAM = better multitasking.
ROM: Read Only Memory. Non-volatile — retains data without power. Contains BIOS/firmware. Cannot normally be changed by user. EPROM/EEPROM can be erased/reprogrammed.

QuestionText: Which of these is an output device?
Explanation: Output devices: monitor, printer, speakers, headphones, projector. Input devices: keyboard, mouse, scanner, microphone, webcam. Both: touchscreen, modem.
Scanner: input device. Converts physical documents/images to digital format. Input: keyboard, mouse, scanner, mic, webcam, joystick. Output: monitor, printer, speaker, projector.
CPU (Central Processing Unit): the brain of the computer. Executes instructions, performs arithmetic and logical operations. Contains ALU (calculations), CU (control), registers.

QuestionText: Hard disk drive (HDD) is a type of:
Explanation: HDD: secondary storage. Non-volatile (data persists without power). Stores OS, applications, user data permanently. Slower than RAM but much larger capacity and cheaper.
SSD: Solid State Drive. Uses flash memory (no moving parts). Faster, more durable, quieter, lighter than HDD. More expensive per GB. No mechanical failure from drops.
1 GB = 1024 MB = 1,048,576 KB = 1,073,741,824 bytes. Storage industry uses 1 GB = 1000 MB (SI), but computing traditionally uses 1024. 1 TB = 1024 GB.

Options: A) A type of hard disk
B) Main circuit board connecting all components
Explanation: Motherboard: main PCB (Printed Circuit Board). Houses CPU, RAM slots, expansion slots, connectors, BIOS chip. Everything connects to motherboard.

QuestionText: A 'printer' is which type of device?
Explanation: Printer: output device — converts digital information to physical printed form. Types: inkjet, laser, dot-matrix, 3D printer. Output: monitor, printer, speaker, plotter.
Optical storage: uses laser to read/write. CD (700 MB), DVD (4.7-8.5 GB), Blu-ray (25-50 GB). Magnetic storage: HDD. Flash/semiconductor: SSD, USB drives, SD cards.

QuestionText: A 'touchscreen' is which type of device?
Explanation: Touchscreen: both input (detects touch) and output (displays images). Used in smartphones, tablets, ATMs, kiosks. Other both I/O: modem, network card, headset.

Options: B) Faster than RAM, used by CPU to store frequently accessed data
Explanation: Cache: ultra-fast memory between CPU and RAM. L1 (fastest, smallest, inside CPU core), L2, L3. Stores frequently used data to reduce CPU-RAM access time. Most expensive memory.

QuestionText: Input devices provide data to the computer. Which is NOT an input device?
Explanation: Plotter: output device (draws vector graphics, technical diagrams). Input devices: barcode scanner, webcam, microphone, keyboard, mouse, joystick, fingerprint sensor.
System software: manages hardware, provides platform for applications. OS, device drivers, utilities (disk cleanup, antivirus), programming tools. Application software: MS Office, Chrome, games.

Options: B) Programs designed for specific user tasks (Word processor, games, browsers)
Explanation: Application (app) software: programs for specific user tasks. Examples: MS Word, Chrome, Photoshop, games, Tally, email clients. Runs on top of system software.

QuestionText: The function of an ALU (Arithmetic Logic Unit) in CPU:
Options: B) Performs arithmetic and logical operations
Explanation: ALU: performs arithmetic (add, subtract, multiply, divide) and logical (AND, OR, NOT, compare) operations. Part of CPU along with Control Unit (CU) and Registers.

Primary (main) memory: directly accessible by CPU. RAM (volatile, working memory) + ROM (non-volatile, firmware). Secondary memory: HDD, SSD, DVD, USB (stored permanently, not directly CPU-accessible).

Options: B) Power supply is cut off
Explanation: Volatile memory (RAM): data lost when power is removed. Non-volatile (ROM, HDD, SSD, USB): data persists without power. This is why you should save your work!

QuestionText: Which port is most commonly used to connect modern devices like USB drives, keyboards, mice?
Explanation: USB (Universal Serial Bus): most common connector. USB-A, B, C, Micro, Mini. Hot-pluggable (connect/disconnect without restart). High speed, provides power. Replaced serial, parallel, PS/2 ports.

QuestionText: 'Booting' requires the computer to first access:
Explanation: Boot sequence: Power ON → BIOS/UEFI (ROM) runs POST → finds bootable device → loads bootloader from HDD → OS loads into RAM. BIOS stored in ROM (non-volatile).

Options: B) Laser is generally faster and cheaper per page for volume printing
Explanation: Inkjet: uses liquid ink, cheaper to buy, better for photos, slower. Laser: uses toner (powder), faster, cheaper per-page for text, better for office use. Inkjet: liquid ink jets onto paper.

QuestionText: Barcode reader is a type of:
Options: B) Input device that reads barcodes
Explanation: Barcode reader: input device using laser/camera to read barcodes (patterns of parallel lines). Used in retail, inventory, libraries. 2D variant: QR code reader.

QuestionText: Bandwidth of memory is measured in:
Options: B) Bytes per second (GB/s for RAM)
Explanation: Memory bandwidth: how fast data can be read from or stored to RAM. Measured in GB/s or MB/s. DDR4 RAM: typically 25-50 GB/s. Higher bandwidth = faster data transfer to CPU.

Options: A) Software that can be easily changed
B) Permanent software programmed into ROM/flash memory of hardware
Explanation: Firmware: software permanently stored in hardware's ROM or flash memory. BIOS, printer firmware, router firmware. More permanent than software but can sometimes be updated (flashed).

QuestionText: Which storage has the fastest access speed?
Explanation: Speed ranking: RAM > SSD > USB Flash > HDD > Optical. SSD has no moving parts → much faster than HDD. NVMe SSDs (PCIe) are even faster than SATA SSDs.

Options: B) High-definition audio/video output to monitors and TVs
Explanation: HDMI (High-Definition Multimedia Interface): transmits uncompressed video and audio. Used to connect computers to monitors, TVs, projectors. Single cable for both HD video and audio.

QuestionText: The function of a GPU (Graphics Processing Unit) is:
Explanation: GPU: specialised processor for rendering graphics, video, 3D. Has thousands of smaller cores for parallel processing. Also used for AI/machine learning (NVIDIA CUDA). VRAM is GPU memory.

Options: B) Gaming and aircraft simulation control
Explanation: Joystick: input device. Controls movement in games, flight simulators, robotic arms. Gamepad/controller: similar but thumb-operated. Mouse: 2D cursor control.

Options: B) Provides battery backup during power cuts
Explanation: UPS: battery backup providing power during electricity cuts. Allows graceful shutdown of computers to prevent data loss. Also conditions power (surge protection).

Options: B) Unique physical/behavioural characteristics (fingerprint, retina, face)
Explanation: Biometric devices: identify people by physical traits. Fingerprint scanner, iris scanner, face recognition, voice recognition. Used for authentication/security.

Options: B) Directs the flow of data between CPU and other components
Explanation: CU: coordinates CPU operations, fetches and decodes instructions, controls data flow between ALU, registers, memory, I/O. The 'manager' of CPU operations.

Options: B) OS automatically detects and configures new hardware
Explanation: Plug and Play: connect device → OS automatically detects, installs drivers, configures. Most modern hardware is PnP. Previously, hardware needed manual IRQ, DMA settings.
Pointing devices: mouse, trackball, touchpad, graphics tablet/stylus, joystick. Used to control cursor. Keyboard = keying device. Scanner = imaging input device.

QuestionText: Storage capacity of a Blu-ray disc is approximately:
Explanation: Storage: CD ≈ 700 MB. DVD ≈ 4.7 GB (single layer), 8.5 GB (dual). Blu-ray ≈ 25 GB (single layer), 50 GB (dual). Named for blue-violet laser (shorter wavelength = more data).

Options: B) Whether data is retained without power
Explanation: Volatile: needs power to retain data (RAM). Non-volatile: retains data without power (ROM, HDD, SSD, flash). Key distinction for data persistence.

Options: B) Physical documents/images to digital format
Explanation: Scanner: input device using light/CCD sensors to digitise physical documents, photos, slides. Types: flatbed, document feeder, handheld. OCR software converts scanned text to editable text.

Options: B) CPU, memory, and I/O devices (data highway of computer)
Explanation: System bus: communication pathway connecting CPU, memory, and I/O devices. Three types: data bus (carries data), address bus (carries memory addresses), control bus (carries control signals).
Projector: output device. Projects computer display onto a screen/wall. Used for presentations, classrooms, home theatre. DLP, LCD, LED projector types. Connect via HDMI/VGA.

Options: B) USB drives, SD cards, SSDs
Explanation: Flash memory: non-volatile, solid-state (no moving parts). Used in USB drives, SD cards, SSDs, smartphone storage, camera cards. Electrically erasable and rewritable.

Options: B) The smallest unit of a digital image/display
Explanation: Pixel (picture element): smallest unit of a digital image. Display resolution described by pixels: 1920x1080 (Full HD) = over 2 million pixels. Higher resolution = sharper image.

QuestionText: What is the purpose of a heat sink on a CPU?
Options: B) Dissipate heat to prevent CPU from overheating
Explanation: Heat sink: metal component with fins placed on CPU. Absorbs and dissipates heat into surrounding air. Often paired with a fan (CPU cooler). Prevents thermal throttling and damage.
PROM: Programmable ROM — can be programmed once after manufacture. EPROM: Erasable (UV light). EEPROM: Electrically Erasable. Flash memory: advanced EEPROM used in modern storage.

Options: B) Number of pixels displayed (width × height)
Explanation: Resolution: number of pixels displayed. 1920x1080 (1080p Full HD). 2560x1440 (1440p/2K). 3840x2160 (4K Ultra HD). Higher resolution = sharper, more detailed image.

QuestionText: A modem connects your home to:
Options: B) Your ISP and the internet
Explanation: Modem: connects home/office network to ISP. Converts digital signals to/from the medium used by ISP (phone lines, cable, fibre). Many home devices combine modem + router.

QuestionText: Which type of memory is directly accessed by the CPU during processing?
Explanation: CPU directly accesses RAM for active data and programs. Data on HDD/USB must first be loaded into RAM. Cache is even faster (L1/L2/L3) but much smaller than RAM.

QuestionText: Keyboard is which type of device?
Explanation: Keyboard: input device. Sends keystrokes to computer. Types: QWERTY, membrane, mechanical, virtual (touchscreen). Special keys: function keys, modifier keys (Ctrl, Alt, Shift).

QuestionText: Which storage medium is read-only (cannot be written to by user)?
Explanation: CD-ROM/DVD-ROM: Read Only Memory — data written at factory, cannot be modified by user. CD-R/DVD-R: Write once. CD-RW/DVD-RW: Rewritable (many times).
PPI: pixels per inch — density of pixels. Higher PPI = sharper image. Retina displays: 300+ PPI. Print resolution: DPI (dots per inch). More PPI in same screen size = crisper text and images.

Options: B) Physical components of a computer system
Explanation: Hardware: physical, tangible components. CPU, motherboard, RAM, HDD, monitor, keyboard. Contrast with software (programs, data). Firmware: intermediate — software embedded in hardware.
